headline: The two short runs back now sit several days cold, with no third to confirm cadence. Big Åre block still anchors the base. Strength and a fresh threshold read remain the open gaps.
confidence_reasons: No recent activity data in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is a big trail block followed by a quiet gap and then two short, genuinely rangey runs — and the calendar has gone quiet again since. The Åre stretch stacked enormous time-on-feet at low intensity, and those two restart runs pulled the average pace and intensity sharply upward, but they haven't been followed by anything, so the weekly rhythm question from earlier this week is still unanswered. Strength stays the thinnest part of the whole picture — a single isolated session in the last four weeks against a year-to-date cadence that used to be far more regular. Steps remain high enough that background load is doing real work even on days without a logged session, so total activity isn't as low as the run log alone implies. The Polar cardio-load "detraining" flag reflects the recent quiet stretch of tracked sessions, not the demonstrated base underneath it — treat it as a comment on the last few days, not on fitness.
sections.trends: Zoom out and the shape is clearly cyclical rather than declining: a massive multi-day trail block, then a deliberate-looking gap, then a small sharp restart. Year-to-date distance is running far ahead of the same point last year, so the medium-term trajectory is genuine accumulation, not drift. The recent four-week block sits well above the prior four purely on the weight of Åre. That's a coherent shape for a year-round hybrid athlete — a durability bolus followed by a return to shorter, faster work — provided the shorter work now actually recurs rather than trailing off.
sections.threshold: The threshold reading is now the oldest signal on the board by a wide margin, and it's aged past the point where the deep base can be assumed to still map cleanly onto it. The two restart runs both reached into higher zones, which is encouraging as indirect evidence the top end is still available, but neither was a sustained tempo that would refresh the number. Right now the honest read is uncertainty: the base is demonstrably intact, but where the lactate turn point actually sits today is a genuine unknown until a controlled sustained effort updates it.
sections.zones: The weekly aggregate is dominated by the Åre block, which was almost entirely low-zone by design — appropriate for a durability effort of that length. The two restart runs are a different animal: both spent real time in the upper-middle zones with brief top-end touches, which reads as mixed-intent rather than cleanly easy or cleanly hard. That grey-zone drift was flagged before and still holds — for a block trying to sharpen speed, a run that sits mostly mid-zone doesn't clearly serve either an easy-recovery or a quality purpose. Neither is wrong occasionally; the thing to watch is whether intent starts separating.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing new worth flagging on the strength HR front — the most recent lift didn't capture heart rate at all, so the quiet corner stays quiet on that dimension too. The earlier strength sessions that did capture HR sat sensibly in the low-to-moderate range for functional work, consistent across sessions. No source-agreement concerns arise from today's data.
sections.calendar: The running streak is intact at its all-time best length, which speaks to weekly consistency even through a block that changed character completely. But within the last stretch the pattern is lumpy: a dense cluster of trail days, a gap, two runs, then quiet again. That lumpiness is fine as an occasional feature of trail-block recovery, but the strength side tells the more concerning consistency story — it has gone from a regular fixture to near-absent, and that's the frequency pattern most worth restoring.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance PBs were all set roughly a year ago in late summer, which is exactly this part of the calendar — so seasonally the athlete may be entering a window where sharpness returns. The restart runs show top-end range is present, but they're too short and too mixed to indicate a 5K or 10K PB is imminent yet. If the shorter runs consolidate into distinct quality sessions, that window becomes realistic rather than hypothetical.

watch_items: Watch whether a third run finally lands to confirm the restart as a rhythm rather than an isolated pair.
Watch for a sustained tempo effort to refresh the now-stale threshold number before assuming the old value still holds.
Watch whether strength returns to any recurring slot — it's now the single most degraded consistency signal in the picture.
Watch whether the short runs separate into clear easy-vs-quality intent instead of settling mid-zone.
